items.q: Do you work with expats and internationals?
items.a: Yes. Supporting internationals and expats is at the heart of my work, and I offer sessions in both English and German. I understand the particular mix of opportunity and pressure that comes with building a life away from home. Whether you are newly arrived, long settled, or somewhere in between, you are very welcome here.

items.q: Can we work together if I live in another country?
items.a: Yes. All sessions take place online by video, so we can work together wherever you are in the world. I see clients internationally and work across time zones by arrangement, based in Central European Time. All you need is a private space and a stable connection.

items.q: Do you understand the challenges of living between cultures?
items.a: Yes. Living between cultures can bring a quiet sense of not fully belonging anywhere, alongside questions of identity, language, and home. Many internationals carry this experience without ever putting words to it. In counselling we can explore what living between worlds means for you and help you feel more settled and at home in yourself.

items.q: Can you help with relocation stress?
items.a: Yes. Relocating can be exciting and exhausting at the same time, bringing practical upheaval, loss of familiar support, and a lot of adjustment all at once. Counselling offers steady support while you find your footing in a new place. Together we can ease the overwhelm and help you reconnect with a sense of stability and direction.

items.q: Do you work with cross-cultural couples?
items.a: Yes. Cross-cultural couples often navigate differences in language, family expectations, and ideas of home, which can add richness as well as friction to a relationship. I work with couples in both English and German and can support you across different locations and time zones online. My aim is to help you understand each other more deeply and build a shared way of living that honours both of you.
